stem: Why do marginal costing and absorption costing give different profits?

options.rationale: Correct: only absorption costing includes fixed overhead in inventory.

options.content: They use different selling prices for the same goods
options.rationale: Selling prices are the same under both methods.

options.content: They use different variable costs of production
options.rationale: Variable costs are the same under both methods.

options.content: They count different numbers of units sold
options.rationale: The units sold are the same under both methods.

explanation: Only the valuation of inventory differs: absorption costing carries a share of fixed production overhead in inventory, marginal costing does not.

stem: In a year when closing inventory is higher than opening inventory, which profit is higher?

options.rationale: Correct: fixed overhead is carried forward in the extra inventory.
Marginal costing charges all the fixed overhead in the year.
They are equal only when inventory is unchanged.

options.content: It depends on the selling price
options.rationale: The comparison depends on the change in inventory units.

explanation: When inventory rises, absorption costing defers part of the fixed overhead in closing inventory, so its profit is higher.

stem: In a year when opening and closing inventory are equal, how do the two profits compare?

options.rationale: That is when inventory rises.
Correct: the fixed overhead carried in equals the amount carried out.
That is when inventory rises as well; here there is no change.

options.content: The difference equals the total fixed overhead
options.rationale: The difference is based on the change in inventory units.

explanation: No change in inventory means no change in the fixed overhead carried forward, so the profits are equal.

stem: Opening inventory is 400 units and closing inventory 900 units. Fixed production overhead absorbed is US\$2.50 a unit. By how much does absorption profit exceed marginal profit?

options.rationale: This multiplies the closing inventory by the rate and ignores the opening inventory.
This multiplies the opening inventory by the rate.
This adds the opening and closing inventory before multiplying.

explanation: Difference = (900 - 400) × 2.50 = US\$1,250. Absorption profit is higher because inventory rose.

stem: Opening inventory is 1,800 units and closing inventory 1,100 units. Fixed production overhead per unit is US\$6. The absorption profit is US\$28,600. What is the marginal profit?

options.rationale: This deducts the difference; marginal profit is the higher figure when inventory falls.
The profits differ when inventory changes.
This uses the opening inventory of 1,800 units instead of the fall of 700 units.

explanation: Inventory fell by 700 units, so absorption profit is lower by 700 × 6 = US\$4,200. Marginal profit = 28,600 + 4,200 = US\$32,800.
hints: When inventory falls, absorption profit is the lower.

stem: Which method must be used to value inventory in published financial statements prepared under IAS 2?

options.rationale: It excludes fixed production overhead, which IAS 2 requires.
Inventory is valued at cost or net realisable value if lower.
Correct: IAS 2 requires inventory at full production cost.

options.content: Either method, at the preference of the manager
options.rationale: IAS 2 does not allow the exclusion of fixed production overhead.

explanation: IAS 2 requires inventory to be valued at cost, including a share of fixed production overhead, so absorption costing is used for external reporting.
hints: Think of which cost includes fixed production overhead.

stem: A manager is paid a bonus based on absorption costing profit. Near the year end she increases production without any extra sales. What is the effect?

options.content: Reported profit falls, because more variable cost is charged
options.rationale: Variable cost of unsold units is carried in inventory.

options.content: Reported profit is unchanged, because sales are unchanged
options.rationale: Absorption profit depends on production through inventory valuation.

options.content: Cash improves, because inventory is an asset
options.rationale: Cash is spent on production and not recovered until the goods are sold.

options.content: Reported profit rises, but cash is tied up in unsold inventory
options.rationale: Correct: more fixed overhead is carried forward, and no cash is received.

explanation: Extra production carries more fixed overhead into closing inventory under absorption costing, raising profit without extra sales. Cash falls.
hints: Where does the fixed overhead of unsold units go?

stem: If inventory falls during the year, absorption costing profit is lower than marginal costing profit.
explanation: True. Fixed overhead from the opening inventory is released into cost of sales.

stem: Over the whole life of a business, total profit under absorption costing is different from total profit under marginal costing.
explanation: False. Overhead deferred in one year is charged in a later year, so the totals are equal over the whole life; only the timing differs.
hints: What happens to deferred overhead in later years?

stem: Match each situation to the comparison of profits.

right.content: Inventory falls, so absorption profit is lower

explanation: The comparison depends on whether inventory rises, falls or stays the same. Sales above production means a falling inventory.

stem: Complete the sentence.

payload.template: The difference in profit = change in {{blank:a}} units × fixed production overhead per {{blank:b}}.

explanation: The profits differ by the fixed overhead carried in the change in inventory units.

stem: Which costing method values inventory at variable production cost only?
explanation: Marginal costing.

stem: A Marondera bakery budgets fixed production overhead of US\$63,000 for 18,000 loaves, so fixed overhead is absorbed at US\$3.50 a loaf. Opening inventory was 600 loaves and closing inventory 1,350 loaves. By how much does absorption costing profit exceed marginal costing profit?
explanation: Rate = 63,000 ÷ 18,000 = US\$3.50. Difference = (1,350 - 600) × 3.5 = US\$2,625. Using the closing inventory alone gives US\$4,725.
workedSolution: 1. Rate = 63,000 ÷ 18,000 = US\$3.50. Difference = (1,350 - 600) × 3.5 = US\$2,625. Using the closing inventory alone gives US\$4,725.
hints: Work out the rate first, then use the change in units.

stem: Marginal costing profit for a year was US\$24,800. Opening inventory was 900 units and closing inventory 1,200 units. Fixed overhead absorbed is US\$3.50 a unit. Calculate the absorption costing profit.
explanation: Inventory rose by 300 units: 300 × 3.5 = 1,050. Absorption profit = 24,800 + 1,050 = US\$25,850.
workedSolution: 1. Inventory rose by 300 units: 300 × 3.5 = 1,050. Absorption profit = 24,800 + 1,050 = US\$25,850.
hints: Inventory rose, so absorption profit is higher.

stem: Absorption costing profit was US\$31,400. Opening inventory was 2,000 units, closing inventory 1,200 units and fixed overhead absorbed is US\$5 a unit. Calculate the marginal costing profit.
explanation: Inventory fell by 800 units: 800 × 5 = 4,000. Marginal profit = 31,400 + 4,000 = US\$35,400.
workedSolution: 1. Inventory fell by 800 units: 800 × 5 = 4,000. Marginal profit = 31,400 + 4,000 = US\$35,400.
hints: Inventory fell, so absorption profit is the lower figure.

stem: Opening inventory was 650 units, production 7,800 units and sales 8,100 units. Calculate the closing inventory in units.
Explain why absorption profit is higher than marginal profit when inventory increases.

points.description: Under absorption costing some fixed production overhead is included in the closing inventory
So less fixed overhead is charged to the year, whereas marginal costing charges all of it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Absorption costing carries part of the fixed overhead forward in closing inventory, so less is charged this year than under marginal costing, and profit is higher.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: A business made equal profits under the two methods in year 1 and had higher inventory at the end of year 2 than at the start of year 2. Describe the effect in year 3 if inventory then falls back to its year 1 level.

points.description: In year 2 absorption profit exceeded marginal profit
In year 3 absorption costing releases the deferred fixed overhead into cost of sales
So in year 3 absorption profit is below marginal profit, and over the three years the totals are equal

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: In year 2 absorption profit is higher because overhead is deferred. In year 3 the deferred overhead is charged, so absorption profit is lower than marginal profit. Over the three years the totals are equal.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: Evaluate which costing method gives the more useful profit figure for judging the performance of a manager.

points.description: Marginal costing profit depends on sales and is not affected by changes in inventory
Absorption profit can be raised by building inventory, which does not improve performance
Absorption costing follows IAS 2 and is needed for external reports
Judgement: use marginal costing or contribution for internal performance and decisions, absorption costing for published accounts

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Marginal profit cannot be raised by producing for stock, so it is a fairer measure of a manager's performance. Absorption profit is needed for external reporting under IAS 2. The business should use marginal figures internally and absorption figures externally.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: Marondera Maize Meal sells bags at US\$20. Variable production cost is US\$11 a bag and variable selling cost US\$1 a bag sold. Fixed production overhead of US\$60,000 is absorbed on a budgeted output of 15,000 bags. Administration expenses are US\$18,000. Opening inventory was 1,000 bags, production 15,000 bags (as budgeted) and sales 14,200 bags.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit under marginal costing.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit under absorption costing.
parts.explanation: Full cost 15 a bag; cost of sales 14,200 × 15 = 213,000; gross profit 71,000; less selling 14,200 and administration 18,000 = US\$38,800.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Full cost 15 a bag; cost of sales 14,200 × 15 = 213,000; gross profit 71,000; less selling 14,200 and administration 18,000 = US\$38,800.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the difference between the two profits using the change in inventory.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Reconcile the two profits and explain why absorption costing gives the higher profit.

points.description: Explain that inventory rose, so fixed overhead is carried forward in closing inventory

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Reconciliation of profits**

|  | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Profit under marginal costing | 35,600 |
| Add: increase in inventory (1,800 - 1,000 = 800 units) × US\$4 | 3,200 |
| **Profit under absorption costing** | 38,800 |

explanation: This item tests both profit statements and the reconciliation when inventory rises.
hints: Full cost per bag = variable cost + fixed overhead rate.

stem: Chitungwiza Candles sells candles at US\$12. Variable production cost is US\$5 and variable selling cost US\$0.50 a candle. Fixed production overhead of US\$40,500 is absorbed on a budget of 9,000 candles (US\$4.50 a candle). Administration expenses are US\$9,000. Opening inventory was 1,650 candles, production 7,500 and sales 8,400. Under- or over-absorbed overhead is charged to the year's profit.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the closing inventory in candles.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit under marginal costing.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the under-absorbed fixed production overhead.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit under absorption costing.
parts.explanation: Sales 100,800 - cost of sales 79,800 - under-absorbed 6,750 - selling 4,200 - administration 9,000 = US\$1,050.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Sales 100,800 - cost of sales 79,800 - under-absorbed 6,750 - selling 4,200 - administration 9,000 = US\$1,050.

points.description: Less: decrease in inventory 900 candles × US\$4.50 = 4,050

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Marginal profit 5,100 less 900 × 4.5 (4,050) = 1,050, the absorption profit.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why absorption profit is lower than marginal profit.

points.description: Inventory fell, so fixed overhead brought forward in the opening inventory was charged to this year
Marginal costing charged only the fixed overhead incurred in the year

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Inventory fell, so fixed overhead carried in the opening inventory was charged to cost of sales under absorption costing; marginal costing charged only this year's fixed cost.

explanation: This item tests a reconciliation when inventory falls and fixed overhead is under-absorbed.
hints: Fixed overhead rate = budget ÷ budgeted output.
Charge the under-absorbed overhead in the absorption statement.
